ja: この設計だと、あとで機能を追加できますか？
en: Can we add features later with this design?
alternatives: With this design, can we add features later?
Can we add more features later with this design?
point: 「できますか」は Can we で文を始める

ja: 先週、チームはコストの問題でマイクロサービス案をやめました。
en: Last week, the team dropped the microservices plan because of cost.
alternatives: The team gave up on the microservices plan last week because of cost.
Last week, the team decided against microservices because of the cost.
point: 案を「やめた」は stopped ではなく dropped や gave up on

ja: このサービスを分割したら、レイテンシがどれくらい増えるか誰か分かる？
en: Does anyone know how much latency we'd add if we split this service?
alternatives: Does anybody know how much extra latency we'd get if we split this service?
Does anyone know how much the latency would go up if we split this service?
point: 間接疑問は how much latency we'd add の語順

ja: リードエンジニアは、この設計が長期的にはうまくスケールしないと最初から気づいていたのかもしれません。
en: The lead engineer may have realized from the start that this design wouldn't scale well in the long run.
alternatives: The lead engineer might have known from the beginning that this design wouldn't scale well long-term.
Maybe the lead engineer realized right from the start that this design wouldn't scale well over time.
point: 過去の推量は may have + 過去分詞、that 節は時制を合わせ wouldn't

ja: このキャッシュ層は、レイテンシを下げるだけでなく、データベースの負荷も大幅に減らしてくれます。
en: Not only does this cache layer cut latency, but it also takes a lot of load off the database.
alternatives: This cache layer not only cuts latency but also takes a lot of load off the database.
Not only does this cache layer reduce latency, it also greatly reduces the load on the database.
point: Not only を文頭に出したら does + 主語の語順に

ja: 僕たちがレビューをやる前に、佐藤さんはもうデータベースの読み取りと書き込みを分ける案を出していたんだよ。
en: Before we held the review, Sato had already suggested separating database reads and writes.
alternatives: Sato had already proposed splitting database reads and writes before we did the review.
By the time we had the review, Sato had already suggested separating reads and writes in the database.
point: レビューより前の出来事なので had suggested

ja: 明日の会議で、この設計のトレードオフについて私から話してもいいですか？
en: Is it okay if I talk about this design's trade-offs at tomorrow's meeting?
alternatives: Can I talk about the trade-offs of this design at tomorrow's meeting?
May I discuss this design's trade-offs at tomorrow's meeting?
point: 「〜してもいい？」は Is it okay if I 〜。if の後は現在形

ja: 両方の案をホワイトボードに書き出してみよう。
en: Let's write both options on the whiteboard.
alternatives: Let's put both options on the whiteboard.
Let's list both options on the whiteboard.
point: 「〜してみよう」は Let's＋動詞の原形で言う

ja: この API の仕様は、フロントエンドチームのレビューが終わるまで確定しません。
en: The API spec won't be finalized until it's been reviewed by the front-end team.
alternatives: The API spec won't be locked in until it's been reviewed by the front-end team.
The API spec isn't going to be finalized until the front-end team has reviewed it.
point: until 節は未来のことでも will を使わず、it's been reviewed とする

ja: 僕たちが去年メッセージキューを選んでいたら、今こんなにタイムアウトで苦労していないはずだよね。
en: If we had chosen a message queue last year, we wouldn't be struggling with these timeouts now.
alternatives: If we'd gone with a message queue last year, we wouldn't be struggling with all these timeouts now.
If we'd picked a message queue last year, we wouldn't be having all these timeout problems now.
point: 過去の条件は had chosen、今の結果は wouldn't be

ja: マイクロサービスのほうが柔軟だとしても、うちくらいの規模のチームには複雑すぎると私は思います。
en: Even if the microservice approach is more flexible, I think it adds too much complexity for a team of our size.
alternatives: Even if microservices are more flexible, I think they're too complex for a team our size.
Even if a microservice architecture is more flexible, I think it's too complicated for a team of our size.
point: 「〜だとしても」は even if で始める

ja: もし彼女が最初にデータ量を見積もっていなかったら、私たちはたぶん間違ったデータベースを選んでいたでしょう。
en: If she hadn't estimated the data volume up front, we would probably have chosen the wrong database.
alternatives: If she hadn't estimated the data volume at the start, we'd probably have picked the wrong database.
We'd probably have chosen the wrong database if she hadn't estimated the data volume first.
point: 過去の仮定は had not 過去分詞、帰結は would have 過去分詞

ja: 元のシステムを作ったチームが勧めたやり方は、来年見込んでいるトラフィックの量を考慮していません。
en: The approach recommended by the team that built the original system doesn't account for how much traffic we're expecting next year.
alternatives: The approach recommended by the team that built the original system doesn't take into account how much traffic we expect next year.
The team that built the original system recommended an approach that doesn't account for the traffic we're expecting next year.
point: 主語が長くても動詞は doesn't で受ける

ja: なぜ田中さんはこの設計を選んだんですか？
en: Why did Tanaka choose this design?
alternatives: Why did Tanaka pick this design?
Why did Tanaka go with this design?
point: 過去の疑問は did を使い、動詞は原形の choose に戻す

ja: 僕たち、もう3週間もキャッシュ層の設計について議論してるのに、まだ誰もベンチマークを取ってないよね。
en: We've been debating the caching layer for three weeks, but nobody has run a benchmark yet.
alternatives: We've been discussing the cache layer design for three weeks, and still no one has run a benchmark.
We've been arguing about the caching layer for three weeks now, yet nobody's done any benchmarking.
point: 続いている議論は現在完了進行形 have been debating

ja: 最初に GraphQL を採用しましたけど、それ以来、開発って本当に速くなったと思いますか？
en: We adopted GraphQL at the start, but do you think it has actually made development faster since then?
alternatives: We chose GraphQL at the beginning, but do you think development has really gotten faster since then?
We went with GraphQL from the start, but do you feel it's actually sped up development since then?
point: since then があるので後半は現在完了 has made

ja: データが増え続けているので、私たちは一覧 API にページングを入れるべきです。
en: We should add pagination to the list API because the data keeps growing.
alternatives: We should add paging to the list API since the data keeps growing.
We ought to add pagination to the list API because the data keeps growing.
point: 「べき」は should。must にすると強すぎる

ja: テックリードに、キャッシュ層を追加する前にトレードオフをまとめてもらうよう頼んでもらえますか？
en: Could you ask the tech lead to write up the trade-offs before we add a caching layer?
alternatives: Can you ask the tech lead to write up the trade-offs before we add a caching layer?
Could you ask the tech lead to lay out the trade-offs before we add a cache layer?
point: ask＋人＋to do。「まとめる」は write up が自然

ja: この案には何かデメリットはありますか？
en: Are there any downsides to this approach?
alternatives: Is there any downside to this approach?
Are there any disadvantages to this plan?
point: Are there any の後は複数形 downsides

ja: 認証まわりを担当しているエンジニアに、この設計を見てもらうよう頼んでもらえますか？
en: Could you ask the engineer handling authentication to take a look at this design?
alternatives: Could you ask the engineer in charge of authentication to look over this design?
Would you ask the engineer who handles authentication to review this design?
point: the engineer handling で後ろから説明、ask 人 to 動詞

ja: 三つの案の中では、Redis を使う案がいちばんシンプルだと思います。
en: I think the Redis option is the simplest of the three.
alternatives: Of the three options, I think the Redis one is the simplest.
I think using Redis is the simplest of the three options.
point: 三つの中で「いちばん」は the simplest of the three

ja: 課金ロジックだけ変更のペースがほかと違うので、サービスを二つに分けることを考えてもらえないかなと思っていたんですが。
en: I was wondering if you'd be open to splitting the service in two, since the billing logic keeps changing at a different pace from everything else.
alternatives: I was wondering whether you'd consider splitting the service in two, since the billing logic changes at a different pace from the rest.
I was wondering if you might consider breaking the service into two, because the billing logic keeps changing at a different rate from everything else.
point: 控えめな提案は I was wondering if で始める

ja: 最初からスキーマの変更履歴を残しておけばよかったと、今ではうちのチームの全員が思っています。
en: Everyone on the team now wishes we had kept a history of schema changes from the start.
alternatives: The whole team now wishes we'd tracked our schema changes from the beginning.
Now everyone on the team wishes we had recorded our schema changes from day one.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を had + 過去分詞に

ja: この案は安いけど、あまり柔軟じゃないです。
en: This option is cheap, but it isn't very flexible.
alternatives: This option is cheap but not very flexible.
This plan is cheap, but it isn't very flexible.
point: 形容詞だけの文にも be 動詞 is が必要

ja: 私たちは今、二つの案を比べているところです。
en: We're comparing two options now.
alternatives: We're comparing two ideas right now.
Right now we're comparing two options.
point: 「今〜しているところ」は be + -ing

ja: 私たちがモノリスに決めたのは、速さじゃなくて運用コストが理由だったんです。
en: It was the operating cost, not the speed, that made us choose the monolith.
alternatives: It was operating costs, not speed, that made us go with the monolith.
What made us choose the monolith was the operating cost, not the speed.
point: It was A, not B, that ～ で理由を強調する

ja: 障害が起きても一つのサービスの中で影響が収まるような設計にできないでしょうか？
en: Couldn't we go with a design where a failure stays contained within a single service?
alternatives: Couldn't we design it so that a failure doesn't spread beyond one service?
Could we design it so that a failure stays contained within a single service?
point: design の後は where でどんな設計かを説明する

ja: そのキャッシュ設計で確定する前に、私たちに少しフィードバックをいただけますか？
en: Could you give us some feedback on the caching design before we commit to it?
alternatives: Could you give us a bit of feedback on the caching design before we lock it in?
Would you mind giving us some feedback on the caching design before we commit to it?
point: feedback は数えられない名詞。a feedback や feedbacks にしない
